adaptation: TypeScript -> ESM JavaScript with every algorithm, limit and diagnostic string preserved.

The three third-party engines are quarantined in `engines.mjs`, the only module in the city tree that names them: each is imported lazily, and a missing install is reported as ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE (an installation problem) instead of as a broken document.

XLSX: the donor's static fflate import becomes `await loadFflate()`, so `readArchiveEntries` is async; the byte-level guards run before the engine load, so obviously wrong input fails closed without depending on engine availability. The donor's `decodeUtf8` maps to the ingestion core's `decodeText`, whose encoding warnings are forwarded rather than dropped.

DOCX: the donor's lazy mammoth import becomes `await loadMammoth()`, and the two injectable converter seams are kept exactly, so the heading/list mapping and the paragraph budgets are provable without the engine.
PDF: the donor's lazy engine import becomes `await loadPdfjs()`, which loads the legacy build (no worker, no DOM). Nothing had to be dropped from the donor's getDocument options.

The synthetic document builders of the donor's test-only `workbook-fixtures.ts` become product code in `samples.mjs`, because a real OOXML package or a real PDF can be assembled in memory and neither a product surface nor a test needs a committed binary fixture.
Error codes are namespaced per reader (NOT_XLSX/CORRUPT_XLSX/TOO_LARGE/ENCRYPTED_XLSX/ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE and the same shape for DOCX and PDF) so a caller can branch without parsing a message.
knownDifferences: Nothing is persisted: the adapters take bytes and return sections, and the module never writes a file.
ENCRYPTED_* codes are preserved from the donor but no engine path raises them here: fflate 0.8.x silently ignores the ZIP encryption flag, and the readers have no password handling to exercise.
No OCR and no page rendering: the PDF adapter extracts text only.
The DOCX adapter emits paragraphs (text and HTML), not a full OOXML document model; anything mammoth cannot express is dropped by the engine, and its messages are mapped to typed warnings.

vectors: XLSX: shared strings, sheet name and part, used range, and rows recovered as a real grid
XLSX: markdown table rendering with a header row and a separator row
XLSX: a formula with no cached value warns and never yields a computed number
XLSX: archive byte, entry count, per-entry and total decompressed size, sheet, row and column limits all fail closed
XLSX: a non-ZIP payload is NOT_XLSX and a corrupt archive is CORRUPT_XLSX
DOCX: paragraph splitting, heading levels (including Chinese headings) and bullet/list mapping
DOCX: paragraph and character budgets produce the donor's truncated behaviour
DOCX: the injectable converter seams drive extraction and HTML mapping without the engine, and mammoth drives it with the engine
DOCX: a non-ZIP payload is NOT_DOCX and a ZIP that is not a DOCX is CORRUPT_DOCX
PDF: %PDF preflight, per-page text, and document info
PDF: byte, page, per-page character and total character limits fail closed before or during extraction
PDF: a truncated or corrupt document is CORRUPT_PDF, never a silent empty result
PDF: ENCRYPTED_PDF is reserved for an engine that reports encryption
all three: extracting the same bytes twice is deeply equal (deterministic)
all three: the module imports only the engine seam, the ingestion core and node: builtins
